Interface IuRefreshableCacheHint<K,V>

Type Parameters:
K - key type
V - value type
public interface IuRefreshableCacheHint<K,V>
Supplies metadata directing how one key interacts with an IuRefreshableCache.

A hint is obtained once per IuRefreshableCache.apply(Object) invocation, before the cache is read, so an implementation should be inexpensive to produce and to evaluate. See IuRefreshableCache for how each method below participates in the lookup lifecycle.

    • DEFAULT

    • CLEAR_ALL

      static final IuRefreshableCacheHint<?,?> CLEAR_ALL
      Clears all cached results after successful refresh, doesn't cache refreshed value.

      Recognized by the cache by identity: only this instance, as returned by clearAll(), triggers an immediate full clear. A distinct implementation that returns true from shouldClear(Object) for every key is not equivalent — it takes the deferred, per-entry invalidation path instead.

    • clearAll

      static <K,V> IuRefreshableCacheHint<K,V> clearAll()
      Clears all cached results after a successful call, and doesn't cache the result of that call.

      Returns the singleton CLEAR_ALL instance, which the cache recognizes by identity in order to clear in line rather than by deferred per-entry evaluation. Prefer this over a predicate that matches every key when a call invalidates broadly: it is a constant-cost invalidation, whereas a deferred hint is re-evaluated by every subsequent cached lookup until it is purged.

      Clearing in line also discards every invalidation still pending, since emptying the cache subsumes them.

      Type Parameters:
      K - key type
      V - value type
      Returns:
      clear-all cache hint: clear all, don't cache, no embedded values

    • shouldClear

      default boolean shouldClear(K key)
      Determines if a key should be cleared from the cache.

      This method serves two distinct purposes, distinguished by which key is passed.

      • Evaluated against the key that produced this hint, before the call, it selects the uncached path: the result is resolved directly and never cached. This is how a key that mutates the backing source is declared.
      • Evaluated against other keys, after that call succeeds, it selects which cached entries the call invalidated. A cleared entry is repopulated by the next caller, which waits for the new value.

      A hint is only queued for invalidation when its call succeeds, so a failed call never discards cached data.

      Implementation Note: during invalidation this method is invoked while the candidate entry's monitor is held, once per queued hint per lookup. It must return quickly, and must not invoke a remote method or touch the cache that produced it.

      Parameters:
      key - key to evaluate; might not be the key that generated this hint
      Returns:
      true if the key should be cleared

    • restore

      default Optional<V> restore()
      Restores a result value resolved elsewhere, typically by another node in the same cluster, in place of calling the cache's refresh function.

      Consulted at the start of every refresh for the key, including the first, so a hint that always restores never contacts the backing source. A restored value short-circuits the refresh function, and is therefore never passed to inspect(Object).

      Not consulted on the uncached path — when caching is disabled, or when shouldClear(Object) returns true for this hint's own key.

      Implementation Note: invoked on a pooled call thread, bounded by the configured call TTL along with the call it replaces.

      Returns:
      restored value; null if no value was restored; empty optional caches a null value

    • inspect

      default Map<K,V> inspect(V result)
      Inspects a cacheable result for cacheable embedded values.

      Each embedded value is published under its own cache key as though it had been resolved directly, allowing one call to populate many entries and reducing load on the backing source.

      Each embedded value must be consistent with the result when read individually from the backing source. Values may fluctuate only between upstream transactions, never within the transaction represented by result. An embedded value that can differ from what a direct read would return must not be published here.

      Implementation Note: invoked on a pooled call thread, only when the result is itself being cached. Returning null or an empty map both mean the result exposes no related values.

      Parameters:
      result - cacheable result
      Returns:
      mapping of embedded values by related cache key
